title: Constructive Bounds for the Topological Expressivity of Neural Networks
why_read: A theoretical math paper on neural network expressivity using topology, interesting mainly to researchers studying the mathematical limits of what networks can represent.
analysis: This paper studies how complex a shape a ReLU neural network's output can be, measured using topological invariants called Betti numbers which roughly count independent loops and holes in a space. The authors give explicit formulas for network architectures (number of layers and neurons) needed to produce outputs with specified topological complexity, improving on prior bounds. This is a niche theoretical contribution relevant to researchers interested in the mathematical foundations of deep learning expressivity rather than practitioners. The conjectured tight bound for sphere-like outputs is an interesting open question but has no immediate practical application.
